div.head: Wi 19
div.ab: Cliroc feowra sum hine clænsie his heafodgemacene ⁊ ane his hand on wiofode; oþre ætstanden, aþ abycgan.
Cliroc feowra sum hine clænsie his heafodgemacene ⁊ ane his hand on wiofode; oþre ætstanden, aþ abycgan.
Cliroc feowra sum hine clænsie his heafodgemacene, ⁊ ane his hand on wiofode; oþre ætstanden aþ abycgan.
Ein Kleriker reinige sich als einer von vieren seiner Standesgenossen und allein seine Hand auf dem Altar; die anderen sollen [nur] dabei stehen [und] den Eid leisten.
A cleric is to clear himself as one of four of his equals in rank, and his hand alone on the altar; the others are [only] to stand by [and] take the oath.
A clerk shall clear himself with [the support of] three of his own class, he alone [having] his hand on the altar. The others shall attend for the purpose of validating the oath.
A cleric is to purge himself with three of the same order, and he alone is to have his hand on the altar; the others are to stand by and discharge the oath.
A cleric should clear himself as one of four of his equals, and his hand alone on the altar; the others should stand by to validate the oath.

note.seg: In minor orders; see Gl Geistliche 1
‘Mit 3’; Toller s. v. feower; ‘vielleicht mit 4’ Wülfing; vgl. Gl Eideshelfer 21. 32. 47
‘With 3’; Toller s. v. feower; ‘perhaps with 4’ Wülfing; cf. Gl Eideshelfer 21. 32. 47
[Ergänze diese Zahl über ‘allein’]. Nicht (mit Wilkins und Toller Suppl. 5a) ‘seine eine Hand’
[Supply this number over ‘allein’]. Not (with Wilkins and Toller Suppl. 5a) ‘his one hand’

standen, abycgan sind Optative mit später Endung. Ein and dazwischen mit Schmid zu ergänzen ist für den Text wohl nicht nötig. — ‘Die Eideshelfer sind mit dem Hauptschwörer durch Handreichung verbunden’; Brunner II 433; sie heissen þe him mid standað; Ath

standen, abycgan are optatives with a late ending. To supply an and between them, with Schmid, is probably not necessary for the text. — ‘The oath-helpers are joined to the principal swearer by the giving of hands’; Brunner II 433; they are called þe him mid standað; Ath

Wie man Ags. að syllan, mlat. sacramentum persolvere sagt, so bedarf abycgan [s. Wb: ‘Strafe zahlen’] nicht der [unzutreffenden] Parallele mit accapian und keiner Emendation; Price empfahl alecgan, Toller Suppl. 5 abyrgan: beides unmöglich

Just as one says in Anglo-Saxon að syllan, in Medieval Latin sacramentum persolvere, so abycgan [see Wb: ‘pay a penalty’] needs neither the [inapposite] parallel with accapian nor any emendation; Price proposed alecgan, Toller Suppl. 5 abyrgan: both impossible
gemacene, a late (12th cent.) form for gemacena. For feowra sum see note on II As. cap. 11.
ane may possibly stand for ana; but cf. cap. 24 below, where ane appears to be instr.
abycgan, perhaps 3rd pl. conjunct. Schmid suggested the insertion of and before aþ.

note.label: cleric
note.seg: Probably includes the positions of doorkeeper, psalmist, reader, exorcist, acolyte, and subdeacon; see discussion under ‘Church and public assembly’ in Commentary to chapter 2.
